sections.heading: What actually happens when a Physics tutor sits at your dining table?
paragraphs: A good session at your table looks almost nothing like a lecture. The tutor arrives, the child's current school paper comes out, and the next sixty to ninety minutes are mostly the child writing while the tutor watches the pencil. The reason this mode suits Cambridge IGCSE Physics is that the subject punishes process errors, and a process error is only visible while it is happening. Once the answer is on the page the evidence is gone.

The physical room does real work. A dining table beats a desk for this subject because there is space to open a past paper, a graph-paper pad, a formula sheet and a calculator at once without stacking them. A hard chair at the right height keeps a child from drawing a ray diagram with their chin on the table, which is how diagrams end up at a slant. A wall within reach takes a small whiteboard or just a sheet of chart paper where the week's relationships live. The kitchen is forty seconds away, which matters more than it sounds: a kettle, a measuring jug, a kitchen scale and a thermometer turn specific heat capacity from a formula into something that happened on the counter. A torch, a glass paperweight and a sheet of paper give a refraction demonstration. A stack of books, a smooth tray and a toy car give an inclined plane. A phone stopwatch, a bit of string and a key give a pendulum whose period the child can time badly, repeat, and learn why repeat readings exist.

What a tutor beside the child catches, and a screen does not, is a list every experienced teacher recognises. The calculator left in the wrong angle mode for an entire question on refraction. The rounding done at step one and carried into step four. The ruler held at an angle so the best-fit line is drawn through two points instead of between all of them. The hand that starts writing an answer, stops, and erases, which is the moment the child does not understand and will never report. The axis labelled without a unit, every single time, until somebody is sitting close enough to say so before the next one. A parent in the next room hears a session going well; a tutor at the table sees it going wrong early enough to fix it.

The home setting also changes what the end of the session can be. A tutor who is physically present can leave something behind: three past-paper questions marked up and clipped to the fridge formula sheet, a graph the child plotted badly with the corrected version beside it, a sticky note on the calculator reminding them to check the mode. They can look at the school's own worksheet and tell you whether the department teaches moments before or after density, which changes what gets taught next week. They can say, in front of you rather than over a message, that the problem this month is not Physics but twenty minutes of attention, and that two shorter sessions would beat one long one. None of that travels well down a video call.
bullets: Child writes, tutor watches the pencil: process errors caught live
Dining table beats a desk: paper, graph pad and calculator open together
Kitchen scale, jug and thermometer make specific heat capacity physical
Torch and glass block for refraction; books and a tray for an inclined plane
Marked questions and a formula sheet left behind on the fridge
Calculator mode, early rounding and unlabelled axes spotted before the habit sets

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one Mumbai exam series
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at the grade. Look at whether the marks that used to leak have stopped leaking. By the fourth session a child who was losing marks to missing units, early rounding and unlabelled graph axes should be losing far fewer of them, and the tutor should be able to show you two scripts side by side to prove it. Content gaps take longer. Four weeks is enough to change habits and to close one or two topics properly, and it is not enough to rebuild a year of Physics.

At one term, the fair question is whether the pattern of errors has changed shape. A child who started the term losing marks everywhere should by now be losing them in a smaller number of identifiable places, and the tutor should be able to name them without checking their notes: nuclear equations, the series-parallel distinction, the gradient-and-area confusion on motion graphs. School assessment marks may or may not have moved by then, because school papers vary enormously in difficulty and one easy terminal flatters everybody. The honest indicator at the term mark is the error list, not the percentage.

At one exam series, you find out. Some children move a long way, some move modestly, and some do not move at all despite a year of sensible weekly work, usually because the problem was never the Physics. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor on the panel is permitted to promise one. What we will do is tell you at four weeks and again at the term mark whether the arrangement is working, which is a less comfortable conversation than an optimistic one but the only useful kind. A tutor who reports nothing but progress every week is not watching closely enough.

When it is not working, say so early and expect it to be handled rather than defended. Tell the coordinator what you are seeing: sessions that drift, homework that never gets set, a child who dreads the doorbell. A replacement profile comes within the week, the new tutor is briefed with the error list rather than starting from zero, and the weekly slot stays where it is so the household routine survives the change. Families who switch at week four lose a fortnight; families who wait until February because they did not want to offend anyone lose the series. Physics (0625) home classes in Mumbai are worth keeping only while they are earning their place in your evening.
bullets: Four weeks: fewer unit, rounding and axis errors, not a grade jump
One term: the error list should be shorter and specifically named
School assessment marks move unevenly because school papers vary in difficulty
Switch at week four rather than in February if sessions are drifting
Replacement tutor briefed with the error list, keeping the same weekly slot

sections.heading: Booking a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 home tutor in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Five things make the first session productive instead of exploratory. The most recent school Physics paper with the teacher's marks still on it, however bad. The school's own syllabus or topic list for the term. A pad of A4 graph paper, because the one in the school bag is always finished. The scientific calculator your child will actually sit the exam with, not a better one borrowed from an older sibling. And the name of the tier your child is entered for, Core or Extended, confirmed with the school rather than guessed at home.

On the logistics side, two things need settling before the tutor leaves the house they live in. The gate: tell your society office the day before, give the name to the watchman or raise the pass on the building app, and ask whether a standing weekly entry can be set up so nobody is waiting downstairs at 6.30 every Tuesday. And the room: clear the table, move the television out of earshot, and plan where a younger sibling will be for the next ninety minutes. Both sound trivial. Both are the reason sessions start fifteen minutes late for a whole term.

The first session itself is diagnostic and should look like it. Expect a short conversation with you about what the school has said, then the child working alone under the tutor's eye through a mixture of questions chosen to expose the four failure types. Expect the tutor to say less than you thought they would. At the end you should get three things in plain language: what is actually wrong, what the first month will cover, and what will be set between sessions. If any of those three is missing, ask for it before the second session rather than after the fourth.

Send the query with your area, your child's year group, the school and one honest sentence about what is going wrong. A coordinator will call the same working day, confirm the tier and your realistic evening window, and come back with the shortlist. You will know the tutor's travel time from their own address to your building before you agree to anything, because on this service that number predicts more than any qualification on the profile does.
bullets: Bring the last school Physics paper with the teacher's marks intact
Have A4 graph paper and the exam calculator on the table

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 home tutor in Mumbai actually charge for?
faqs.answer: The rate reflects five things, and no honest answer exists without them. IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and tier, since Extended supplement teaching asks more of a tutor than Core; on subject scarcity, because experienced 0625 Physics teachers are thinner on the ground than Maths or English teachers; on travel distance, since a tutor crossing two suburbs is paid for the hour they spend on the Western Express Highway as well as the one at your table; on session length and frequency, where a committed twice-weekly slot usually prices better per hour than ad-hoc sessions; and on timing, with the January to March mock window the tightest. IB Gram quotes against your actual address and tier rather than publishing a list.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Kharghar or Panvel for a 7pm Physics slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is based in Navi Mumbai. A Kharghar or Panvel address is matched to a tutor in Kharghar, Belapur, Nerul or Vashi, all a short run along Palm Beach Road or the Sion-Panvel Highway, and a 7pm weekday slot holds comfortably. What does not hold is a tutor brought across the creek from the island city or the Western Suburbs for the same slot. The Atal Setu has made that journey far quicker than it was, but quicker is not reliable at 6pm, and an arrangement that depends on a clear run will break by the second month. For a weekday evening we match inside the node.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get past our society gate every week?
faqs.answer: The same way any regular service provider does, and it is worth setting up properly in week one. Give the society office or the main gate the tutor's full name and phone number, and ask whether your building allows a standing weekly entry for a recurring visitor rather than a fresh pass each time. Most larger complexes do, either in the register or on the building app, and it saves ten minutes of waiting downstairs every session. Buildings that run vendor verification should put the tutor through it; a tutor who objects is telling you something useful. Keep the visitor log intact rather than waving them through, because a weekly record of who entered and when is worth having.

faqs.question: Can home tuition fix Paper 6 when there is no lab at my house?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the part parents underestimate. The alternative to practical is a written paper about experiments, not a practical exam, so almost all of the marks come from pencil skills: reading an instrument to the right precision, tabulating consistently, choosing a sensible graph scale, plotting accurately, drawing a best-fit line, taking a gradient, spotting an anomaly and writing a real precaution. All of that is table work. Where apparatus genuinely helps, a kitchen covers more than you would expect: a measuring jug, a kitchen scale, a thermometer, a torch, a glass block, a stopwatch, string and a stack of books handle density, specific heat capacity, refraction and pendulum timing between them.

faqs.question: We are in Thane off Ghodbunder Road. Is a weekday evening slot realistic in the monsoon?
faqs.answer: Realistic, with a fallback agreed in advance. A Thane tutor living near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening crawl, and a heavy monsoon spell makes the Ghodbunder stretch worse again. So we match Thane addresses to Thane tutors, occasionally to a Mulund tutor crossing the Eastern Express Highway, and we write the wet-weather plan into the arrangement from week one: either the session moves to a fixed Saturday morning or it runs online that week. Deciding that in advance is what stops a monsoon fortnight from quietly becoming the end of the arrangement.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell the coordinator and ask for a replacement; it is a normal request and it is handled in days, not weeks. Describe what you are actually seeing rather than giving a verdict: sessions that drift into chat, no work ever set between visits, your child going quiet whenever the subject comes up, the same topic explained three times. A new profile is sent within the week, and the incoming tutor is briefed with the error list the first one built so your child is not starting from the beginning again. The weekly slot stays in the same place so the household routine survives. Switching at week three costs you a fortnight; waiting until February costs you the series.

faqs.question: Is online better than a home tutor for Physics 0625?
faqs.answer: For this subject, usually not as the main session, though it is genuinely good as a supplement. The practical-skills paper and the diagram work are pencil tasks, and a tutor beside your child sees the ruler angle, the calculator mode and the hesitation before an answer is erased. Online loses all three. What online wins is reach and flexibility: the strongest Extended supplement specialist available to you may live in a different zone entirely, and a mark-scheme walkthrough the night before a mock does not need anyone to travel. The arrangement most families settle on is a home visit for the core weekly session with online used for the extras.

faqs.question: Does my child need to remember every formula for 0625?
faqs.answer: Not every one, but far more than most children assume, and this is a reliable source of lost marks. Cambridge supplies some relationships and expects the rest from memory, so a question handing over a mass, a specific heat capacity and a temperature change expects the thermal energy relationship to appear without prompting. The fix is mechanical rather than clever: ten minutes at the start of each session writing out every relationship from memory on a blank sheet, and whatever fails to arrive goes onto a single sheet on the fridge door, where it gets read dozens of times a week without anybody studying. Check the current subject guide for which relationships are supplied.

faqs.question: What should the study space at home look like for these sessions?
faqs.answer: A hard chair at a table in a shared room, with the door open and the television out of earshot. A dining table works better than a bedroom desk for Physics because you need a past paper, a graph pad, a formula sheet and a calculator open at the same time without stacking them. Chair height matters more than it sounds: a child hunched over the table draws ray diagrams at a slant, and slanted diagrams lose angle marks. Keep a small whiteboard or a sheet of chart paper on a wall within reach for the week's relationships, plan where younger siblings will be for the next ninety minutes, and keep phones in another room.

faqs.question: How much progress is realistic after four weeks?
faqs.answer: Habit change, not a grade change. By the fourth session the marks that were leaking to missing units, rounding at the wrong step and unlabelled graph axes should have largely stopped leaking, and your tutor should be able to put two of your child's scripts side by side and show you where. One or two content topics will be properly closed. A year of accumulated gaps will not be, and anyone suggesting otherwise after four weeks is selling rather than teaching. Ask at the four-week mark for the current error list; if it is shorter and more specific than it was in week one, the arrangement is working.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: An adult in the flat is the sensible standard, though they do not need to be in the room. Sessions run in a shared space with the door open, and a parent nearby is both the right safeguarding habit and useful for the two minutes at the end when the tutor reports what happened. Being in the room for the whole session tends to work against the teaching, because children answer to the parent instead of thinking. If both parents work late, a grandparent or any responsible adult at home covers it, and the slot can be moved to a weekend morning instead. What does not work is a session with the child alone in the house.

faqs.question: How do I judge whether a Physics tutor is actually good?
faqs.answer: There is no such thing as the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai in the abstract; there is only the right one for your child's tier, timetable and address. Judge from the trial session on three things. Ask them to explain the critical angle in two minutes without drawing anything, and listen for whether they describe a property of a boundary or wave their hands at a beam of light. Ask what the last three IGCSE students they taught struggled with, because thin experience gives vague answers. Then watch them mark five minutes of your child's own work: a good tutor explains why the mark was lost, a weak one just corrects the answer. No honest tutor promises a specific grade.
